name: UIListLayout
simple: A UIListLayout automatically lines up all the UI objects next to it in a neat row or column, so you don't have to set each one's Position. Drop it inside a Frame, and every other UI object in that Frame gets stacked in order. It can also stretch items to fill space ('flex') and wrap onto new lines.
analogy: A UIListLayout is like a teacher saying 'line up!' Everyone in the room (the frame) stands in one neat line, in order, with the same gap between them.
whenToUse: A column of menu buttons (Play, Settings, Quit)
A row of tabs or icons
Lists inside a ScrollingFrame, like a shop or leaderboard
Toolbars where buttons should share space evenly (flex)
where: Put it inside the container (usually a Frame or ScrollingFrame) whose children you want lined up. It arranges its SIBLINGS. Works the same whether made in Studio or with Instance.new in a LocalScript.

terms.modifier: A small invisible object you put INSIDE a UI object to change how it looks or behaves. It does nothing on its own.
terms.parent: The object something is placed inside. A modifier affects its parent.
terms.sibling: Objects that share the same parent, like brothers and sisters.
terms.UDim: Half of a UDim2: just one Scale and one Offset. UDim.new(0, 8) means 0% + 8 pixels. UDim.new(0.1, 0) means 10% of the parent's size.
terms.Scale: A fraction (0 to 1) of the parent's size. 0.5 = half.
terms.pixel: One tiny dot on the screen.
terms.LocalScript: A script that runs on the player's own device. UI code goes in LocalScripts.
terms.Vector2: Two numbers together: X (width or left-right) and Y (height or up-down).
terms.layout: Automatic arranging of UI objects so you don't place them by hand.
terms.FillDirection: Which way the list goes: Vertical (top to bottom, default) or Horizontal (left to right). It comes from UIGridStyleLayout, the base of UIListLayout.
terms.SortOrder: How items are ordered: LayoutOrder (by each item's LayoutOrder number, default) or Name (alphabetical).
terms.LayoutOrder: A number on each UI object. With SortOrder LayoutOrder, lower numbers come first.
terms.padding: Empty space. In a list, the gap between items.
terms.flex: A mode where items stretch or spread out to fill the leftover space in the container.
terms.cross-direction: The other direction from the list. For a top-to-bottom list, the cross-direction is left-right.
terms.wrap: When items run out of room, continue on a new row or column.

examples.title: A neat column of menu buttons
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local playerGui = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screenGui.Parent = playerGui

local menu = Instance.new("Frame")
menu.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
menu.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
menu.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(220, 200)
menu.BackgroundTransparency = 1
menu.Parent = screenGui

local layout = Instance.new("UIListLayout")
layout.FillDirection = Enum.FillDirection.Vertical
layout.SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder
layout.HorizontalAlignment = Enum.HorizontalAlignment.Center
layout.Padding = UDim.new(0, 10) -- 10 pixels between buttons
layout.Parent = menu

local names = {"Play", "Shop", "Settings"}
for i, name in names do
	local button = Instance.new("TextButton")
	button.Name = name
	button.Text = name
	button.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(200, 50)
	button.LayoutOrder = i * 100 -- 100, 200, 300
	button.Parent = menu
end
explain: The UIListLayout is inside menu, so it arranges menu's other children: the three buttons.
We never set the buttons' Position. The layout stacks them: first at y = 0, next at 50 + 10 = 60, next at 120.
LayoutOrder 100, 200, 300 sets the order. Gaps of 100 let you slip a new button in later (like 150).
Padding UDim.new(0, 10) is a 10-pixel gap. UDim.new(0.05, 0) would be 5% of the menu's height instead.

gotchas: The layout controls Position, so changing a child's Position does nothing. Change LayoutOrder to reorder.
Children are sorted by LayoutOrder by default. If they all have the same LayoutOrder (0), they fall back to the order they were added.
Hidden children (Visible = false) are skipped, and the others close the gap.
Put the UIListLayout INSIDE the container, as a sibling of the items, not inside one of the items.
A UIAspectRatioConstraint or UISizeConstraint on an item overrides its size in the layout.

UIListLayout.HorizontalFlex.simple: For a left-to-right list: how leftover sideways space is shared. None (default) = items keep their width. Fill = items stretch to fill the whole width. SpaceBetween = gaps only between items. SpaceAround = equal space on both sides of each item. SpaceEvenly = equal gaps between and around. In a top-to-bottom list, Fill makes every item as wide as the container.
UIListLayout.HorizontalFlex.example:
local layout = script.Parent -- a UIListLayout
layout.FillDirection = Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal
layout.HorizontalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment.Fill -- buttons share the full width

UIListLayout.ItemLineAlignment.simple: In flex mode, lines items up across the list's direction within each line. Start = top (or left), Center, End = bottom (or right), Stretch = fill the whole line, Automatic (default) = follow HorizontalAlignment/VerticalAlignment.
UIListLayout.ItemLineAlignment.example:
local layout = script.Parent
layout.FillDirection = Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal
layout.ItemLineAlignment = Enum.ItemLineAlignment.Center -- items centered up-and-down in the row

UIListLayout.Padding.simple: The gap between items, as a UDim. UDim.new(0, 10) is 10 pixels. UDim.new(0.05, 0) is 5% of the container's size in the list's direction (5% of a 400-pixel-tall frame = 20 pixels).
UIListLayout.Padding.example:
local layout = script.Parent
layout.Padding = UDim.new(0, 8) -- 8 px between items

UIListLayout.VerticalFlex.simple: For a top-to-bottom list: how leftover up-and-down space is shared. None (default), Fill (items stretch to fill the height), SpaceBetween, SpaceAround or SpaceEvenly. In a left-to-right list, Fill makes every item as tall as the container.
UIListLayout.VerticalFlex.example:
local layout = script.Parent
layout.FillDirection = Enum.FillDirection.Vertical
layout.VerticalFlex = Enum.UIFlexAlignment.SpaceEvenly -- spread items out evenly

UIListLayout.Wraps.simple: When true, items that don't fit continue on a new row (or column), like words wrapping in a sentence. When false (default), they keep going past the edge.
UIListLayout.Wraps.example:
local layout = script.Parent
layout.FillDirection = Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal
layout.Wraps = true -- make new rows when a row is full
UIListLayout.Wraps.gotcha: Wrapping and flex need a little extra work from the game, so don't use them on huge lists if you don't need them.
